cells.expected: The supplied OPPO run should identify the same device branch as the backend report before being used as a PDBM00 result.
cells.observed: The directory metadata identifies OPPO PKB110 / Android 16, not OPPO PDBM00 / Android 9. Its harness also cannot find InstantGameActivity, and its final screenshot is a system/battery dialog rather than a game frame; it is adjacent evidence only.

cells.expected: Once the host Activity is available, the exact package shows the Graphics first frame and accepts the ordinary touch core loop.
cells.observed: Neither supplied failed run reaches the game frame, and no package SHA is shown; the game renderer branch cannot be assigned as the cause or cleared from this evidence.

confirmedFindings: TapTap build 196126 reports two Android startup failures and no performance metrics for this report.
ZTE A2022P exact supplied logs reproduce a TapTap host crash and missing InstantGameActivity before a game frame is observed.
OPPO PDBM00 is a backend-table branch without raw logs; the supplied OPPO raw directory is PKB110 and must not be substituted.
The current evidence does not establish whether the package, TapTap client/plugin, or device-specific host environment owns the crash.
remainingGaps: No ZIP SHA-256 is shown in the TapTap report or device directories, so the failed report cannot be bound to the current package b224cd5470efb70e1de7d63f9361f7269835e4bf7adaa53123e76d67dfe24173.
ZTE logcat omits the exception stack body after FATAL EXCEPTION, preventing a precise host root-cause classification.
OPPO PDBM00 needs a matching raw logcat/autotest run; PKB110 is not an acceptable substitute.
No exact-package natural first-frame, touch, terminal or replay evidence exists for either failed device.
